faq.q: What is the origin of Abdelkader?
faq.a: The name is Arabic and is a compound of عبد and a second element.
Yes. The underlying compound is عَبْدُ الْقَادِر (ʿAbd al-Qādir).

faq.q: What is the root of Abdelkader?
faq.a: عبد is related to ع ب د; al-Qādir is related to ق د ر (q-d-r).
Abdelkader is a traditional Muslim personal name because it contains a compound invoking al-Qādir, a divine epithet in Islamic tradition.
This record does not establish Abdelkader as an explicitly named Qur'anic person; the compound's religious meaning is distinct from personal-name attestation in the text.

faq.a: In Urdu, the name means servant of the Able/Powerful; the compound combines عبد with al-Qādir.
The supplied “ab-del-ka-der” is an approximate pronunciation; local pronunciations vary.

faq.a: The record classifies the name as masculine, consistent with traditional usage; regional frequency data is not supplied.
